text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--Danish shipowners are ordering four out of five new vessels from foreign yards, mainly in the far east.
--Danish shipowner Ole Lauritzen intends to set up a ferry service from Roedby to Puttgarten in Germany, to rival state railways' Scandlines.

--Opposition Conservative and Liberals want Social Affairs Minister Karen Jespersen taken to task for her ministry's award of tenders to a company on which ministry officials make up about half of the board.
--Denmark is one of the European countries in which it is cheapest to fire staff.
--A growing number of analysts believe that share prices, making new records every day of late, are nearing their peak.
--The government wants to cut spending by making private employers pay their workers' sick pay for the first three weeks of illness, instead of the present 14 days, before the state takes over.
--House sales are running at the same level as in the record year of 1996, but more buyers are coming on to the market and prices are expected to flatten out.
--Consumer confidence is growing. Danes have more money and are willing to spend more but are also saving part of their increased income.
--Swedish and German insurance companies are preparing an offensive on the high-priced Danish market. Winners in the expected price war will be the consumers.
--Swedish telecoms operator Telia is starting tests of a new GSM 1800 mobile phone system on Danish customers in the Odense area. REUTER SCW
